name: Jeremy Moss
current_role: President pro tempore of the Michigan Senate
bio: Jeremy Moss is a Michigan state senator from Southfield who has served as president pro tempore of the Michigan Senate since 2023. He previously served on the Southfield City Council (2011-2015), in the Michigan House (2015-2019) and in the state Senate's 11th district (2019-2023). He holds a degree in journalism and political science from Michigan State University.

platform.point: Lower costs for Oakland County families by confronting corporate price gouging.
Hold the Trump administration accountable and defend the rule of law.
Protect voting rights, civil rights and access to reproductive health care.
Has sponsored legislation adding LGBTQ protections to Michigan civil rights law.

economy.evidence: Campaign centres on cracking down on corporate price gouging and tax relief for seniors and working families.

welfare.evidence: Campaign pledges to resist threats to Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid.

liberty.evidence: Backed expanded reproductive-freedom protections and LGBTQ civil-rights protections, alongside gun safety laws.

foreign.evidence: Supports Israel and a two-state solution while opposing Prime Minister Netanyahu.

name: Ethan Baker
bio: Ethan Baker has been mayor of Troy, Michigan, since 2019, after being elected to the Troy City Council in 2015. He moved to Oakland County about 17 years ago and describes himself as a nonpartisan-minded leader.

platform.point: Reduce national division by listening and engaging across differences.
Rebuild public confidence in how government institutions work.
Keep communities safe and expand economic opportunity for families.

notes: The campaign site lists broad themes but no specific policy positions.

name: Rashida Tlaib
bio: Rashida Tlaib has represented Detroit-area districts in the U.S. House since 2019, first MI-13 and now MI-12. She served in the Michigan House from 2009 to 2014 and earlier worked as a lawyer at the Sugar Law Center. She was raised in Southwest Detroit and holds degrees from Wayne State University and Cooley Law School.

platform.point: Pursue economic and housing justice, including tax credits for working families through the BOOST Act.
Restore civil rights protections and end qualified immunity through the Justice for All Act.
Advance environmental justice with cleaner air, water and infrastructure.
Expand health care to everyone through Medicare for All.
Bar TSA data sharing with ICE for deportation enforcement via the No TSA Data for ICE Act.

economy.evidence: Supports raising the minimum wage to $18-20 an hour and taxing the wealthy.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion rights and recreational marijuana, while backing universal background checks on gun sales.

security.evidence: Sponsored police accountability measures, seeks to end qualified immunity and asked to abolish the federal death penalty.

immigration.evidence: Early supporter of abolishing ICE and backs a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants.

foreign.evidence: Sponsored a bill to remove US forces from Yemen and calls for ending US aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: Supports expanding renewable energy and phasing out fossil fuels.

education.evidence: Opposes school vouchers and supports tuition-free higher education.

name: James Hooper
current_role: Tradesman and Wayne County Republican Committee chairman
bio: James D. Hooper is a tradesman from Detroit's east side who has worked in Eastern Market and the building trades and chairs the Wayne County Republican Committee. He has done mission rebuilding work in Liberia. He ran for this seat in 2022 and was the Republican nominee in 2024.

platform.point: Protect life from conception to natural death.
Oppose any infringement on Second Amendment rights.
Expand parental rights in education and eliminate the federal Department of Education.
Lower taxes and cut regulation and bureaucracy to support American jobs.
Secure the border and stop illegal immigration.
Keep a well-trained, well-equipped military focused on defense.

economy.evidence: Calls for lower taxes and fewer regulations on business.

welfare.evidence: Favours free-market approaches to health care.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion from conception, while opposing gun restrictions and vaccine mandates on individual-autonomy grounds.

immigration.evidence: Prioritises border control and opposes illegal immigration.

foreign.evidence: Supports a well-trained and well-equipped military focused on national defense.

education.evidence: Backs parental rights in education and abolishing the federal Department of Education.

notes: Welfare score is based on a brief free-market health care statement.

name: Donavan McKinney
bio: Donavan McKinney is a Detroit native who has served in the Michigan House of Representatives since 2023. Before holding office he worked as a legislative director, community engagement specialist and health care union organizer, and he holds a public policy degree from the University of Michigan. He won the August 2026 Democratic primary for MI-13 over incumbent Shri Thanedar.

platform.point: Raise taxes on billionaires, protect union rights and living wages, and create a universal basic income.
Pass Medicare for All including dental, vision and mental health, plus a national homes guarantee.
Enact a Green New Deal and expand renewable energy and public transit.
End cash bail and qualified immunity and reform sentencing.
Create a pathway to citizenship and close for-profit detention centers.
Shift Pentagon spending to domestic needs and end military aid to Israel.

economy.evidence: Calls for higher taxes on billionaires, living wages and a universal basic income.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All, free college and expanded early childcare.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, wants federal codification and repeal of the Hyde Amendment via the EACH Act.

security.evidence: Supports ending cash bail and qualified immunity and shifting funds to social services.

immigration.evidence: Backs a pathway to citizenship for all immigrants and closing for-profit detention centers.

foreign.evidence: Favours diplomacy first, less Pentagon spending and ending unconditional weapons funding.

energy.evidence: Supports a Green New Deal and a transition to renewable energy.

education.evidence: Wants to fully fund public schools and make college and trade school free.

notes: The earlier Commons photo is credited to the City of Detroit with only a Public Domain Mark, so it was not used under the photo rules.

name: T.P. Nykoriak
bio: T.P. (Taras) Nykoriak is the Republican nominee for Michigan's 13th congressional district. He has run for office several times before.
notes: No campaign website or published policy positions were found.

name: Brad Finstad
bio: Brad Finstad has represented Minnesota's 1st congressional district since 2022 and grew up on his family's farm in Brown County. He served in the Minnesota House from 2003 to 2009 and was USDA Rural Development director for Minnesota from 2017 to 2021. He chairs a House Agriculture subcommittee on nutrition, foreign agriculture and horticulture.

platform.point: Cut red tape, pursue balanced budgets and restore fiscal discipline.
Promotes the Working Families Tax Cuts enacted in 2025.
Pursue energy independence using nuclear, oil, gas, biofuels and renewables.
Strengthen rural hospitals and clinics and expand telehealth.
Keep parents central and move education decisions to states and localities.

economy.evidence: Supports tax cuts, less regulation and balanced budgets, and voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

welfare.evidence: Voted for the 2025 reconciliation law that added Medicaid work requirements and SNAP changes.

foreign.evidence: Backed Israel after the 2023 Hamas attack, endorsed 2026 Iran strikes and opposed a war powers limit.

energy.evidence: Backs an all-of-the-above approach including oil and natural gas; voted against the Inflation Reduction Act.

education.evidence: Emphasises parental rights and state and local control over a federal approach.

notes: The campaign website could not be loaded, so it was left blank.

name: Jake Johnson
bio: Jake Johnson is a math teacher from Stewartville in southern Minnesota. He describes growing up poor and working his way into the middle class. This is his campaign for Minnesota's 1st congressional district.

platform.point: End tariffs and cut red tape for housing and childcare to lower costs.
Fund tax cuts for working families with higher taxes on corporations and the wealthy.
Support term limits, a congressional stock trading ban and a lobbyist ban.
Support a balanced budget amendment and oppose debt ceiling increases.
Pass a farm bill, protect right to repair and reverse Medicaid and SNAP cuts.
Pause data center construction until key protections are guaranteed.

economy.evidence: Wants higher taxes on corporations and the wealthy and opposes tariffs, but also backs a balanced budget amendment.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare and reverse Medicaid and SNAP cuts.

foreign.evidence: Calls for ending the war with Iran.

tech.evidence: Supports a moratorium on data centers until protections are in place, and right-to-repair rules for farmers.

notes: The new foreign score rests on one statement about ending the Iran war.

name: Matt Little
bio: Matt Little is a lawyer from Lakeville, Minnesota, whose practice focuses on medical malpractice and personal injury cases. He served on the Lakeville City Council, was mayor of Lakeville from 2012 to 2016 and served in the Minnesota Senate from 2017 to 2021.

platform.point: Pass Medicare for All to make care affordable for everyone.
Remove ICE agents from Minnesota and replace ICE with an agency bound by constitutional limits.
Regulate data centers to protect Minnesota water and farmland.
Tax the ultrawealthy so working Americans pay less.
Make childcare affordable so parents do not have to choose between work and children.
Support police training alongside accountability for unnecessary force.

economy.evidence: Supports taxing the ultrawealthy and expanding the Child Tax Credit.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and affordable childcare.

liberty.evidence: Supports reproductive rights and LGBTQ protections.

security.evidence: Opposes police staffing cuts and funds training while seeking accountability and limits on qualified immunity.

immigration.evidence: Wants to replace ICE with an agency under constitutional limits and require agent identification.

foreign.evidence: Supports ending US military aid to Israel and a two-state solution.

tech.evidence: Calls for regulating Big Tech data centers over water and farmland concerns.

name: Eric Pratt
bio: Eric Pratt has served in the Minnesota Senate since 2013, including terms as assistant majority leader and majority whip. He previously served on and chaired the Prior Lake-Savage school board and worked in banking and financial risk management. He grew up in Prior Lake and holds degrees from the University of Colorado Boulder and the University of St. Thomas.

platform.point: Lower costs, support small businesses and stabilise the economy for working families.
Back law enforcement and first responders with consistent enforcement up to the border.
Crack down on fraud and abuse in government programs.

security.evidence: Campaign emphasises backing law enforcement and first responders.

immigration.evidence: Calls for consistent law enforcement extending to the border.

notes: The campaign site links social accounts without readable URLs, so none are listed.

name: Kelly Morrison
bio: Kelly Morrison is an OB-GYN from Minneapolis who has represented Minnesota's 3rd congressional district since 2025. She served in the Minnesota House from 2019 to 2023 and the Minnesota Senate from 2023 to 2024, holding assistant majority leader roles in both chambers. She sits on the House Small Business and Veterans' Affairs committees.

platform.point: Protect abortion access, building on the pro-choice laws she helped pass in Minnesota.
Bring her experience as a physician to health care policy, including through the Democratic Doctors Caucus.
Lists the economy, environment, health care, small business and veterans as focus areas.

liberty.evidence: On abortion, she helped pass pro-choice legislation in Minnesota and campaigned on reproductive freedom.

notes: Her official issue subpages could not be loaded, so most positions remain empty. The campaign photo URL is a header image and may not be a tight headshot.

name: Tyler Bass
bio: Tyler Bass is a Minnesota business owner who has run companies in fitness, contracting and insurance. He previously held a Minnesota life and health insurance license.

platform.point: Secure the border and deport all immigrants in the country illegally.
Vote against bans on AR-15 rifles and magazine capacity limits.
Close H-1B visa loopholes and put American workers first.
Reduce federal influence that pushes up local property tax bills.
Promote fully underwritten individual health policies priced on personal risk.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on lowering property taxes and reducing federal influence on them.

welfare.evidence: Favours individually underwritten, risk-based private health coverage.

liberty.evidence: On guns, he pledges to oppose AR-15 bans and magazine limits; no other liberty issues are addressed.

immigration.evidence: Calls for deporting every illegal immigrant and curbing H-1B visas.
